source.title: Model multitasking: Can a model learn two different tasks simultaneously through Grokking?

record.file_problem: Figure images are not present in the supplied text; figure captions and textual descriptions are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports a replication of the one-layer modular-addition experiment and its progress measures, then applies them to a dual-task setting.
record.gate_note: The post describes results from its own single-task and dual-task runs. Statements describing results of the cited papers are not recorded as this study's findings. It says the dual-task excluded and restricted losses did not make sense, so no outcomes for those measures are recorded in that setting.
record.test_reason: The post replicates the one-layer modular-addition grokking experiment and its progress measures with the original recipe and three seeds, then extends it to a joint addition and subtraction task. The post is not itself an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author also claims grokking is robust, extending to multitask learning. They say progress measures still give insight in the multitask case, and that the dual-task internals may hint at superposition of generalizing solutions. All of this is framed as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: The author describes the single-task experiment as a replication of the cited progress-measures work, using a one-layer transformer on modular addition and three seeds. The extension concatenates addition and subtraction tasks, adds an operator token, and lowers P from 113 to 79 to keep the dataset size roughly comparable; the author describes some dual-task analyses as hacky.
record.method_sensitivity: The dual-task setup showed less pronounced grokking than the single-task setup. Omitting the operator token changed the result: the model reached only ~ 86% training accuracy and grokking did not occur.

fits_no_version.finding: The dual-task model uses different dominant key frequencies per task (28 for addition, 8 for subtraction). Its key frequencies vary more in strength, with cosine/sine asymmetry and multiple periodicities in the embedding SVD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multitask modular arithmetic, the network forms distinct or superposed Fourier circuits per task rather than one shared circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: Without the operator token, the dual-task model reaches only ~86% training accuracy and never groks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking requires a well-defined input–output mapping; ambiguous inputs prevent memorization and generalization.

record.problems: The text reports averages over three seeds without uncertainty estimates or seed-level results. The author says the dual-task excluded and restricted losses did not make sense because of the dataset and analysis methods, and identifies further analysis as future work.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; one data fraction per setup.
Direct measurement of memorization removal (cleanup) in the post's own runs. Excluded and restricted losses, and the timing of progress measures, for the dual-task model.
All: non-algorithmic data, initialization scale or weight norm.
All: weight decay, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
Whether seeds converge to the same frequencies or algorithm; not compared.

missing.what: Timing of the progress measures. Excluded loss rises during circuit formation while train and test loss are flat. Restricted loss declines before test loss, with a clear inflection before grokking.
Three-phase split (memorization, circuit formation, cleanup) drawn on the post's own averaged 3-seed loss curves.

record.verdict_notes: Informal blog replication (BlueDot project). There are no uncertainty estimates and no seed-level results; figures are unavailable, so verdicts rest on the author's text. The dual-task analysis is self-described as hacky. The removed V2 limits_scope label was based on the analysis failing, which is untested ground rather than a qualifying result.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of training-set size on the delay was not tested; the post reports one dataset size for each task setup.
The post does not report its own direct measurement that memorizing components are removed later. Excluded and restricted losses were not usable for the dual-task analysis.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or weight-norm changes were not tested.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data was not tested.
Weight decay, low-norm circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, and ungrokking were not tested.
The post reports runs with multiple seeds but does not compare whether they converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Optimizer instability and floating-point or softmax artifacts were not tested.

rows.value: Training accuracy reached perfection at ~ 300 epochs; test accuracy gradually met training accuracy after roughly 18,000 epochs (> 99%). The post says grokking was to a lesser extent than in the single-task setting.
